decision_precedence.condition: unresolved_sev1 == 0 and unresolved_sev2 == 0 and substantive_evidence_sufficient == true

amendment_rationale: First release. A crypto claim and its verification are unusually close together: the chain is immutable, hash-addressed, independently retrievable and free to query, so almost every quantitative claim a project makes is checkable against state rather than taken on trust. RBM-003 exists to make that check the default and to record, per claim, whether it was reproduced from chain state or merely asserted. Its gates target the specific ways a checkable claim still misleads: counting one entity as many, verifying supply against a website rather than a contract, and reporting headline liquidity that would not survive an exit.

chain_gates.name: Chain-observable verification
chain_gates.requirement: Every quantitative claim must be reproducible from chain state at a stated block height, by a query recorded in the finding. A claim that cannot be reproduced is ALLEGED and can never establish occurrence.
chain_gates.failure_mode: A dashboard figure is cited as though it were chain state. Dashboards apply undisclosed filters, and the number cannot be regenerated by anyone else.

chain_gates.name: Address distinctness
chain_gates.requirement: Counts of users, holders or actives must exclude self-transfers, cyclic flows, and clusters funded from a common source. An address is not a person.
chain_gates.failure_mode: Ten thousand addresses funded sequentially from one wallet are reported as ten thousand users. This is the sentinel defect in another costume: distinct identifiers that are not distinct entities.

chain_gates.name: Supply and lock verification
chain_gates.requirement: Circulating supply, vesting schedules and locks must be read from contract state, never from a website or a spreadsheet. An unlock schedule is code.
chain_gates.failure_mode: Published tokenomics and deployed contract disagree, and the published version is the one everyone models.

chain_gates.name: Contract authority
chain_gates.requirement: Identify every address that can mint, pause, upgrade, blacklist or withdraw, and the threshold required. A claim of immutability must be verified against the deployed contract and its proxy admin.
chain_gates.failure_mode: 'Ownership renounced' is stated while an upgradeable proxy retains an admin who can replace the implementation entirely.

chain_gates.name: Liquidity reality
chain_gates.requirement: Liquidity must be assessed as exit cost at a stated size, not as headline TVL. Locked, incentivised and self-owned liquidity is identified separately.
chain_gates.failure_mode: TVL is reported as though it were depth. The question a holder actually faces is what it costs to leave, and that is a different number.

chain_gates.name: Provenance and reproducibility
chain_gates.requirement: Every figure records chain, block height, contract address and the exact query, and reproduces on a clean run against an archive node.
chain_gates.failure_mode: A figure is correct when taken and unreproducible a week later, because the block height was never recorded. A number that cannot be regenerated is a claim, not a measurement.
